auditor_version: 2026-11-22; review based on frozen case contracts and data/semantic/commerce_schema_metric_contract_v1.md

evidence: commerce.web_traffic.date is DATE; EXTRACT(YEAR)=2024 selects calendar 2024. SUM(sessions) is grouped by month and traffic_source. DATE_TRUNC returns a timestamp representation of each month start; scorer v3.3 compares it literally against Gold date strings, so row-value equivalence is not established by this audit.

The observed expression EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (delivery_date - ship_date)) is invalid for PostgreSQL DATE subtraction in this frozen schema; the execution trace confirms UndefinedFunctionError. The failed expression cannot produce the requested average duration.

The approved schema contract declares commerce.returns as one row per return_id, so COUNT(*) is equivalent to COUNT(DISTINCT return_id) at this table grain. The SQL filters return_date to calendar 2025 and groups by month. Output alias and timestamp/date representation are assessed separately by output/result scoring.

The query first sums net order-item value at order_id and month grain, filters order_status=delivered and calendar year 2025, then averages delivered order totals by month. This matches the requested average delivered order value.

The query counts customers joined by ZIP to geography, filtered to Hai Phong, age_group 25-34, and signup_date in 2024. The approved schema contract declares one customer per customer_id and one geography row per ZIP, so COUNT(*) preserves distinct-customer count.
The query sums revenue and COGS from sales rows in 2024 where the row-level condition cogs > revenue holds. Aggregates and scope match the request.
The query sums refund_amount by non-NULL return_reason for calendar year 2024. The alternative output alias does not change the selected metric, population, grouping, or time scope.

The query counts rows in commerce.orders, whose approved schema grain is one row per order_id, filtered to calendar year 2025, paid_search and mobile. The row count therefore matches the requested order count.

The SQL selects product_id and catalog p.cogs, orders by p.cogs DESC then product_id ASC, and limits to 5. It is semantically aligned with the requested top five catalog COGS ranking; execution was blocked by a ranking-validator rejection, which is reported separately.

The request and frozen Gold use the snapshot-stored inventory.segment. The observed SQL groups by commerce.products.segment, a current catalog attribute with no historical validity, so it can assign historical snapshot quantities to the wrong segment.

The request and frozen Gold define delivered orders by orders.order_status and scope the year using orders.order_date. The observed SQL instead filters shipments.delivery_date and does not constrain orders.order_status or order_date; it changes both population and time semantics.

The query sums return_quantity by the destination city reached through returns.order_id -> orders.zip -> geography.zip and filters by return_date in 2025. Ordering is not semantic for this unordered case.
The query sums return_quantity by product_id over [2023-01-01, 2026-01-01), which includes calendar years 2023 through 2025 and excludes 2026.
The query averages all review ratings grouped by the current products.category using the approved product_id join. This matches the explicit current-category and all-history request.
The query sums recorded payment_value by payment_method for payment rows whose linked order_date is in calendar 2025. This preserves the requested recorded-payment metric and date basis.

The query calculates AVG(shipping_fee) and COUNT(shipping_fee) by destination city for shipments with ship_date in 2025. Joining orders to geography uses the approved destination ZIP path; COUNT excludes NULL fees as requested.

The request is snapshot-scoped and the approved historical dimension is inventory.category. The observed SQL groups by current products.category, which can disagree with the category recorded on the snapshot row.

The approved inventory grain is one row per (snapshot_date, product_id). The query groups by snapshot_date, counts distinct products with non-NULL days_of_supply and separately counts products whose days_of_supply is NULL, preserving NULL rather than coercing it to zero across the inclusive snapshot range.

The request requires matching products across exactly two snapshots and computing before, after, and after-minus-before. The observed SQL returns individual snapshot_date/product_id/stock_on_hand rows and does not pivot, require presence in both dates, or calculate the delta.

The query sums stock_on_hand separately for each snapshot_date within [2025-09-30, 2025-12-01), so it does not sum balances across dates. The products join is many-to-one under the approved product_id key and does not alter inventory grain.

The request explicitly asks for category stored in each inventory row. The observed SQL groups by current products.category, which can disagree with historical inventory.category; it also returns unrequested total/non-null/null count outputs.

This follow-up inherits the prior 2025 order_source statistic. The observed SQL retains order_source and filters delivered status but drops the inherited 2025 order_date range, changing the population to all years.
This follow-up inherits snapshot 2025-10-31. The observed parameter is 2024-11-21, so it ranks a different snapshot; it cannot answer the requested contextual follow-up.
